item: Hardware reasons, forensics notes and the reader page read in the page's language (row 206, part 2)
key_paths: src/shared_text.py; src/llm/backend.py; src/monitoring/forensics.py; src/static/reader.js; configs/server_text_unkeyed.tsv; tests/test_server_text_keyed.py
summary: said() gains nested frames (a hole holds another frame) and said_frames() (parts joined by a space); the page helper renders each part through the locale and labels the whole English when any part is not held, and frame_of() wraps another payload's untranslated English so it is labelled too. Keyed x12 (39 keys): AI hardware capability reasons and the probes' own reasons, session forensics methods and reasons, the reader's tone and mindmap notes. reader.js gets rdSaidHtml, a port of ooSaidHtml the node test checks against it case by case; the raw-print list is now page-built text only. A zero-slack per-file ratchet (configs/server_text_unkeyed.tsv: 1023 bare English caveats, methods and reasons in 265 files, most report text; dict values, keywords and subscript assignments) only goes down. Lesson from the Opus read: a template of holes and punctuation alone translates to itself, and the page reads an unchanged translation as a missing one, so a translated sentence was labelled English in seven languages; the key test now refuses such templates.
